https://www.theguardian.com/australia-ne.text: Former NSW police officer Beau Lamarre-Condon has been accused of fatally shooting Sydney couple Jesse Baird and Luke Davies. Photograph: James Gourley/EPA View image in fullscreen Former NSW police officer Beau Lamarre-Condon has been accused of fatally shooting Sydney couple Jesse Baird and Luke Davies. Photograph: James Gourley/EPA New South Wales Jesse Baird ‘petrified’ of Beau Lamarre-Condon and kept repeating ‘he has a gun’, court hears Friend sobs in witness box and tells Sydney murder trial Baird was scared to go to the police Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Kat Wong Tue 22 Sep 2026 22.21 EDT Last modified on Tue 22 Sep 2026 22.38 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Jesse Baird was “petrified” of Beau Lamarre-Condon because he was an armed police officer who could make a false allegation that would ruin his career, a court has heard. Lamarre-Condon has been accused of fatally shooting Sydney couple Jesse Baird, 26, and Luke Davies, 29, with a police service weapon at Baird’s Paddington home on 19 February 2024. The 31-year-old pleaded not guilty to two counts of murder and one charge of aggravated break and enter. Lamarre-Condon developed an “obsession and infatuation” with Baird, which manifested in compulsive actions during their brief relationship, the prosecution alleged. By the time Baird decided he wanted to end things in November 2023, the behaviour had escalated. Former cop Beau Lamarre-Condon argues self-defence in double murder trial, citing struggle over gun Read more Corey-Dean Thorpe, who had previously been in a years-long relationship with the 26-year-old and remained close friends, began sobbing in the witness box as he told the trial how Baird felt. “He was petrified,” Thorpe told the New South Wales supreme court. “I’d never heard him so scared in his voice before. “He just kept repeating, ‘he has a gun’.” Sign up for the Breaking News Australia email Baird told Thorpe he was “extremely scared” of Lamarre-Condon because he had a gun and was a member of the police force, the court heard. Asked by crown prosecutor Brett Hatfield SC if the 26-year-old had said he was scared to go to the police because Lamarre-Condon was a police officer, Thorpe agreed. Baird was also worried Lamarre-Condon would make a false allegation against him that would “ruin his career”, Thorpe said. Because he was a television presenter on children’s show Totally Wild and an AFL umpire, he needed a certification to work with children, the court heard. Baird sent messages to Thorpe asking for advice on how to break up with Lamarre-Condon. Baird told Thorpe he was worried about what would happen when he ended things “because of the gun and because the accused had stalked and controlled him”, the prosecutor alleged. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | When needed Sign up to Breaking News Australia Get the most important news as it breaks after newsletter promotion On 3 February 2024, months after the break up, one of Baird’s best friends asked if he had heard from Lamarre-Condon. He said Baird had replied: “No, thank fuck, I’m so done with him”. “Once I move house, this will be the last piece of me that Beau knows.” Baird confirmed his new relationship with Davies to his best friend soon after during their last phone call together. “He was almost falling in love with him,” the friend told the court. “I’d never seen Jesse as happy with Luke as what I’d seen him ever. There was something about Luke that just lit Jesse up: they were the real deal.” Lamarre-Condon’s defence team has claimed the police officer was acting in self-defence when he disguised himself as an Uber Eats driver and entered Baird’s home on 19 February. Defence lawyer John Stratton SC argued a struggle had ensued which led to the shots that killed Davies and Baird. The trial before justice Natalie Adams continues. https://www.thewestmorlandgazette.co.uk/.text: Royal Mail Business Cumbria Cumbrian MPs pile pressure on Royal Mail over letter delays Royal Mail Business Cumbria By Gabriel Stewart Reporter Share 0 Comments 3 Skip to next photo 1 / 1 Show caption 1 / 1 Share 0 Comments This article is brought to you by our exclusive subscriber partnership with our sister title USA Today, and has been written by our American colleagues. It does not necessarily reflect the view of The Herald. Two South Cumbrian MPs have piled pressure on Royal Mail over the ‘appalling state of affairs’ that have left Cumbrians missing hospital appointments because of letter delivery delays. Tim Farron, MP for Westmorland and Lonsdale, and Michelle Scrogham, MP for Barrow and Furness, have united in their critique of the company after it was revealed that residents had missed key appointments and bills because of letters being delivered weeks late. One Kendal resident, Sarah Ross, whose children have additional needs, reported how she had missed their appointments because the appointment letters had not arrived in time. Mr Farron said: “It’s an appalling state of affairs that people are missing hospital appointments and people are being penalised for paying bills late because of huge delays in letter deliveries. “Our hard-working posties are being stretched to the limit and desperately need more support. “I recently met with senior management from Royal Mail to challenge them over these issues. “Staffing shortages is a significant problem here which is why they are trying to recruit more posties. But they will struggle to do so unless they offer full-time hours.” Michelle Scrogham and Tim Farron both critiqued Royal Mail's services (Image: Submitted/Tom Cockburn) A Royal Mail spokesperson acknowledged short-term pressures sometimes caused delays and said they are recruiting more staff locally and investing £500m nationally over five years to improve reliability. The company’s latest figures show 84.8 per cent of First-Class letters are delivered the next working day in the LA postcode, below the 93 per cent target set by postal regulator Ofcom. Mr Farron added: “I will keep working to try and fix these problems.” Mrs Scrogham said the state of Royal Mail’s service locally is one of the most regularly raised issues on the doorstep and that “residents deserve a postal service they can rely on”. She said: “This is a problem created by Royal Mail bosses, not by their hard working and dedicated posties and sorting staff. “I've contacted Royal Mail leadership time and again about the terrible service in our area. I’ve met with them, shared the experiences of residents, suggested possible solutions, and requested improvement plans. Michelle Scrogham MP with Michael Hogg, Senior Public Affairs Manager at Royal Mail (Image: Michelle Scrogham MP) “I met them again this week and asked them once more to explain how they will restore reliable deliveries, improve staffing in Barrow and Furness, meet service standards, and ensure vital mail arrives on time. I was not convinced by their answers. Ofcom, the postal regulator, launched an investigation into Royal Mail earlier this year after it missed annual delivery targets yet again. Last October, Ofcom fined Royal Mail £21m for missing annual delivery targets, the third-biggest financial penalty it has ever issued to any company. Royal Mail has not hit its Ofcom-mandated delivery target for first-class post since 2017, or for second-class mail since 2020. Mrs Scrogham added: “Fines have not worked after three consecutive years of penalties and a fourth investigation now underway. But nothing seems to change. The service is still not good enough. “That’s why I recently joined with several MPs to write to Ofcom to say that they now need to act to force Royal Mail to admit the problem and fix it. All options need to be on the table including the threat of bigger fines, and a review of their royal charter.” The Czech billionaire Daniel Křetínský completed a £3.6bn purchase of Royal Mail’s owner, International Distribution Services, last year. A Royal Mail spokesperson said: “ We know how important it is that customers receive their mail when expected, particularly important items such as hospital appointments. “Mail continues to be delivered across Kendal every day, although individual routes can occasionally be affected by short-term pressures. When this happens, our teams work to deliver any outstanding mail as quickly as possible. “We are also recruiting for a number of roles at Kendal Delivery Office to further strengthen the local team.” On top of the £500m investment nationally, they said they were also rolling out a new delivery model across all of their 1,200 delivery offices.
